messages:
zara_p: hi everyone, excited to be here! quick onboarding q: i'm testing streaming locally with the python SSE example and after ~8s the client gets 429s. should i switch to the hosted org key or is there a dev/sandbox key I should use for interactive testing?

ojas: welcome :wave: Use the sandbox/dev key for interactive work. Hosted keys are for prod/staging and map to different quota pools. Sandbox streaming limits are smaller and tuned for interactive dev, but that still explains your 429s.

zara_p: thanks. Console only shows 1 key under my profile labeled "Org API Key" though. is sandbox somewhere else?

carmen: Console -> Settings -> API keys -> toggle the Org dropdown, then look for the "Dev / Sandbox" section. If you don't see it, usually means no sandbox credits or provisioning delay. Ping #infra-ops or submit the compute quota/provision form and ask for a new-hire sandbox key.

keys-bot: Tip: 429 responses include a rate_bucket field, e.g. "rate_bucket=sb_dev_fairshare" and sometimes a Retry-After header. Include both when filing a ticket. Quota form: https://intranet.redwood/company-forms/compute-quota

ojas: also check whether you're using SSE vs websocket. Sandbox streaming over SSE can be throttled differently than websocket streams. If you're hitting a low bucket, try reducing client concurrency and max_tokens while iterating.

zara_p: the 429 body I saw: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","rate_bucket":"sb_dev_fairshare","retry_after":5}. Is that enough for infra to act on?

infra_ops: that's perfect. When you open the quota/provision ticket include that JSON, sample requests-per-minute, and whether it's SSE or WS. If you need a short demo window we can issue a temporary dev bump for N hours.

carmen: quick local best-practices: 1) use a .env and .env.sample so keys don't get committed, 2) prefer short-lived dev tokens for demos, 3) replay recorded streams via a local proxy when iterating heavy UI interactions.

zara_p: awesome, i'll file the form and paste the 429 JSON in the ticket. one more: any recommendations for rotating the sandbox key?

ojas: sandbox keys can be rotated in Console same as hosted. For extra safety put sensitive keys into your OS keyring or use short-lived tokens from the Console "Create ephemeral token" flow. For org-private work we sometimes use a dedicated dev pool with higher dev throughput - infra can advise.

keys-bot: Welcome, zara_p! :tada: Links: Dev keys guide - https://intranet.redwood/docs/dev-keys • Streaming notes (SSE vs WS) - https://intranet.redwood/docs/streaming-guide • Quota requests - https://intranet.redwood/company-forms/compute-quota

zara_p: thank you all, super helpful. i'll open the ticket and ping #infra-ops if it doesn't show up. :thumbsup:
